replicated_originals.reference: Stange, Graydon & Dixon (2017b) Increased urge to gamble following near-miss outcomes may drive purchasing behaviour in scratch card gambling

A.reason: Authors (Stange, Graydon, Dixon) and year 2017 match exactly the reference list's Stange et al. (2017b), the study whose urge-rating pattern and urge-purchase association this pre-registered study explicitly sets out to replicate; the record lacks a title and DOI but identifies the same work as B (Stange et al. 2017a has a different author list).

B.reason: This is Stange et al. (2017b); the paper calls itself a pre-registered replication and extension of it, reproducing its scratch-card paradigm with a larger sample (near-miss urge > loss urge replicated; the urge-by-purchase interaction was not). The 2016 year is the online-first date of the 2017 print article.

notes: A and B are the same original (Stange, Graydon & Dixon, J Gambling Studies, online 2016 / print 2017). Stange et al. 2016 and 2017a are cited for paradigm and background; the bet-size and illusion-of-control hypotheses are new extensions.
